- **Conceptual correctness:** 11
- **Conceptual completeness (advisory, not auto-applied):** 5

## Convergence — the completeness audit/apply loop is spinning

This loop is spinning — the same region keeps re-surfacing without shrinking. Consider the remedy below before continuing; the diagnosis prints the hand-run recipe, but the one-command remedy is `plan-tool convergence deferred-concept-signoff-gate --apply-split` (in-place re-split) or `plan-tool convergence deferred-concept-signoff-gate --apply-scope-out` (carve the step out), behind the same apply-or-recommend gate.

```
convergence: spinning — deferred-concept-signoff-gate (window 3)
  completeness: spinning (4 audits)
  • three-state-navigation: recurs in 2 of 3 audits; severity high → high (peak high)
  • invalid-sidecar-handling: recurs in 2 of 3 audits; severity high → high (peak high)
The decomposition itself is wrong across steps; re-seed and re-decompose:
  plan-tool create deferred-concept-signoff-gate --from-existing <seed.md> --iterate
  Hand-author <seed.md> from the plan's current state (annotate can forward-seed it), then re-run the line above.
```

## Conceptual correctness — fix these first

Unsound or contradictory concepts in the plan's design — the highest-priority gaps, addressed before the completeness gaps below. The audit reports these but does not apply them (read-only-audit split, #85): the paired apply verb walks them first, before the completeness gaps. Address them with:

    plan-tool completeness-apply deferred-concept-signoff-gate   # walk + apply each correctness gap, then the completeness gaps
    plan-tool reconcile-plan-walk deferred-concept-signoff-gate  # alternative interactive review/apply

- HIGH `[three-state-navigation]`: step 4 (`Wire the concept sign-off gate into create`) says “`navigate_concepts` toggles `include`↔`defer` only; `wont_do` comes from the emit,” while Architecture §C and step 3 (`Add the interactive navigate_concepts walker`) require the cycle “`include → defer → wont_do → include`.” Implementing step 4’s stale constraint would prevent operators from choosing or restoring `wont_do`, breaking the promised three-state gate and `## Out of scope` rendering.
- HIGH `[invalid-sidecar-handling]`: step 1 (`Add the concept-tree sidecar leaf`) says a present invalid sidecar must “raise a dedicated `ConceptTreeIntegrityError`,” but step 5’s Input says `read_concepts` is “fail-soft (`None` on anything wrong),” step 5’s Gotcha says malformed content should “recover through the same cold-start derivation path,” and step 8’s Input likewise says “`None` on a missing or unreadable sidecar.” Those consumers can silently replace or ignore a corrupted machine contract instead of stopping or emitting `concept-integrity`, contradicting Architecture §§A/G.
- MEDIUM `[concept-coverage]`: Architecture §E defines coverage as a title/feature cross-reference against “step titles, `features`, and detail bodies,” and says detail supplies a “richer coverage-match corpus,” while step 6 (`Add the two completeness concept checks`) defines matching only through step titles, feature ids, and `Plan.features` titles. A concept represented only in its owning detail body will be reported as uncovered despite the body’s explicit coverage rule.
- HIGH `[scope-out-forward-seed]`: Architecture §H and its structural-remedy acceptance test require a flipped concept to appear as “a `## Deferred` bullet in `render_carved_seed`,” but step 7 (`Make scope_out_step flip…`) specifies a separate “`## Deferred concepts` heading.” Step 8’s deterministic bootstrap recognizes existing `## Deferred` bullets, so the step-7 format can lose the deferral when the carved seed is replanned or later bootstrapped.
- HIGH `[concept-node-identity]`: Step 1 (`Add the concept-tree sidecar leaf`) defines identity as a hash of “title + parent path,” while step 8 (`Add the standalone scope-review command`) promises `--rederive` will add hierarchy while preserving existing decisions. Moving an existing concept beneath a newly emitted parent changes its parent path and therefore its id, so the append-by-id merge cannot recognize it and may append an unsigned duplicate instead of preserving its decision; duplicate sibling titles also produce identical ids and paths.
- MEDIUM `[unattended-signoff-preservation]`: Step 3 (`Add the interactive navigate_concepts walker`) says `--yes` and non-TTY leave sign-off false, and step 8 (`Add the standalone scope-review command`) tests that such a run persists “every node `signed_off=False`.” On a current tree this clears existing operator approvals even when no state changed, contradicting Architecture §C’s rule that approval is invalidated by a changed decision.
- HIGH `[create-emit-failure]`: Step 4 (`Wire the concept sign-off gate into create`) says an unparseable emit should “skip the rest of the gate cleanly — no tree, no overwrite,” and under `--iterate` “an empty fallback is tolerated,” while the Acceptance criteria require the former silent drop to “surface it as a `defer`-suggested concept node.” This failure path finalizes a plan without the machine record or operator gate and can silently discard the very concepts the feature must preserve.
- HIGH `[detail-candidate-parse-failure]`: Step 5 (`Wire the concept sign-off gate into detail`) says “Malformed candidate output is fail-soft for that result,” while its Acceptance criteria require “Every detail-generation result” to emit everything routed to `## Deferred`. A malformed candidate block can therefore leave deferred prose outside the concept tree and consolidated sign-off, recreating the ungated deferral path the plan promises to eliminate.
- HIGH `[scope-out-signoff]`: Architecture §C says “Before persisting any changed decision, it invalidates that node’s prior approval,” and Architecture §A says sign-off applies to “each node’s own current state,” but step 7 (`Make scope_out_step flip…`) requires an `include → defer` transition to “preserve both” `signed_off` and `signed_off_at`. An unattended `scope-out --apply` can consequently convert an approved inclusion into an approved deferral without operator sign-off on that new state.
- HIGH `[tree-prose-rendering]`: Steps 5 (`Wire concepts into detail…`) and 8 (`Add the standalone scope-review command`) mutate `concepts.json` without updating plan prose, contradicting Architecture §A’s “tree is source of truth” and Acceptance’s “`## Out of scope` / `## Deferred` plan sections are rendered from the tree.” Step 8’s detail only says “Save the merged tree” and “Render the outcome,” meaning the plan can retain stale scope prose after an operator changes a decision.
- HIGH `[detail-post-authoring-include]`: Step 5 (`Wire the concept sign-off gate into detail`) performs its consolidated review only after detail bodies have already routed candidates to `## Deferred`; if the operator changes a candidate to `include`, the step neither re-authors the affected detail nor removes the deferred text, leaving the supposedly authoritative tree contradicted by the completed artifact.

## Conceptual completeness — reported, not auto-applied

Coverage gaps in the plan's own ideas (orphaned concepts, uncovered risks, dangling criteria, missing edge cases). Each is a scoping judgment call, so the audit's iterate loop does **not** touch them — chasing every newly-surfaced gap would never converge. Walk and apply them with the paired subcommand:

    plan-tool completeness-apply <plan>                # interactive walk over every gap
    plan-tool completeness-apply <plan> --anchor <slug> # address one gap by its `[slug]`

Each finding below carries the exact `--anchor` value plus the command pre-filled — copy-paste to address it.

- MEDIUM `[unattended-signoff-preservation]`: step 3 (`Add the interactive navigate_concepts walker`) and step 8 (`Add the standalone scope-review command`) require `--yes` or non-TTY execution to leave “every node `signed_off=False`,” but the bundle never distinguishes newly suggested nodes from unchanged nodes carrying an existing operator approval. Re-running `scope-review -y` on a current signed tree can therefore erase valid signoff without any state change or operator decision.
  - Address: `plan-tool completeness-apply deferred-concept-signoff-gate --anchor unattended-signoff-preservation`
- HIGH `[tree-prose-rendering]`: Architecture §A declares the tree the source of truth and says `state=defer` is “rendered into `## Deferred`” and `state=wont_do` into “`## Out of scope`,” but only step 4 (`Wire the concept sign-off gate into create`) rewrites those plan sections. Steps 5 (`Wire concepts into detail`) and 8 (`Add the standalone scope-review command`) persist later state changes without re-rendering the plan, leaving the human-facing prose stale and reopening the Risks entry’s “Two sources of truth” failure.
  - Address: `plan-tool completeness-apply deferred-concept-signoff-gate --anchor tree-prose-rendering`
- HIGH `[structural-remedy-coverage]`: Architecture §H and the structural-remedy Acceptance criterion promise coverage survives split, merge, and re-ground, but no implementation step owns the required split feature partitioning or verifies existing actuators provide it; step 7 (`Make scope_out_step flip…`) explicitly defers “The other three structural remedies.” At HEAD, `launcher.py:escalate_to_split` accepts replacements from `create.py:_propose_step_split`, whose response shape omits `features`, so `_apply_step_split` cannot partition the original feature ownership and a formerly covered concept can become uncovered.
  - Address: `plan-tool completeness-apply deferred-concept-signoff-gate --anchor structural-remedy-coverage`
- HIGH `[rederive-conflicts]`: Step 8 (`Add the standalone scope-review command`) promises `--rederive` will “flag conflicts for explicit operator review,” but `ConceptNode` has no conflict field and step 3 (`Add the interactive navigate_concepts walker`) accepts only a `ConceptTree` and displays state, title, hierarchy, and rationale; neither step specifies a transient conflict set, conflict marker, or resolution rule. The command can preserve an old decision while giving the operator no indication that refreshed evidence suggested a different state.
  - Address: `plan-tool completeness-apply deferred-concept-signoff-gate --anchor rederive-conflicts`
- MEDIUM `[concept-coverage]`: Architecture §E promises “guaranteed coverage” and the Overview says an included concept “can never be silently dropped,” while step 6 (`Add the two completeness concept checks…`) explicitly leaves matching to an implementer-selected title/feature slug heuristic and says to “prefer a false negative.” A semantic omission can therefore pass whenever an unrelated committed step shares the concept’s slug, and a real omission can remain silent, so the stated guarantee exceeds the designed signal.
  - Address: `plan-tool completeness-apply deferred-concept-signoff-gate --anchor concept-coverage`

recommendations.body: step 1 (`Add the concept-tree sidecar leaf`) says a present invalid sidecar must “raise a dedicated `ConceptTreeIntegrityError`,” but step 5’s Input says `read_concepts` is “fail-soft (`None` on anything wrong),” step 5’s Gotcha says malformed content should “recover through the same cold-start derivation path,” and step 8’s Input likewise says “`None` on a missing or unreadable sidecar.” Those consumers can silently replace or ignore a corrupted machine contract instead of stopping or emitting `concept-integrity`, contradicting Architecture §§A/G.
recommendations.suggested_action: make every consuming detail adopt step 1’s distinction—only absence returns `None`; invalid persisted content raises integrity failure and must never trigger cold-start derivation

recommendations.title: Architecture §E defines coverage as a title/feature cross-reference against “step titles, `features`, and detail bodies,
recommendations.body: Architecture §E defines coverage as a title/feature cross-reference against “step titles, `features`, and detail bodies,” and says detail supplies a “richer coverage-match corpus,” while step 6 (`Add the two completeness concept checks`) defines matching only through step titles, feature ids, and `Plan.features` titles. A concept represented only in its owning detail body will be reported as uncovered despite the body’s explicit coverage rule.
recommendations.suggested_action: extend step 6’s authoritative coverage contract and tests to include current detail bodies when present while retaining title/feature matching for bare plans

recommendations.title: Architecture §H and its structural-remedy acceptance test require a flipped concept to appear as “a `## Deferred` bullet
recommendations.body: Architecture §H and its structural-remedy acceptance test require a flipped concept to appear as “a `## Deferred` bullet in `render_carved_seed`,” but step 7 (`Make scope_out_step flip…`) specifies a separate “`## Deferred concepts` heading.” Step 8’s deterministic bootstrap recognizes existing `## Deferred` bullets, so the step-7 format can lose the deferral when the carved seed is replanned or later bootstrapped.
recommendations.suggested_action: make step 7 render flipped concepts through the canonical `## Deferred` concept thread, or explicitly bridge and preserve `## Deferred concepts` across seed parsing and cold-start derivation

recommendations.title: Step 1 (`Add the concept-tree sidecar leaf`) defines identity as a hash of “title + parent path,” while step 8 (`Add the
recommendations.body: Step 1 (`Add the concept-tree sidecar leaf`) defines identity as a hash of “title + parent path,” while step 8 (`Add the standalone scope-review command`) promises `--rederive` will add hierarchy while preserving existing decisions. Moving an existing concept beneath a newly emitted parent changes its parent path and therefore its id, so the append-by-id merge cannot recognize it and may append an unsigned duplicate instead of preserving its decision; duplicate sibling titles also produce identical ids and paths.
recommendations.suggested_action: Define a rederive merge identity and collision policy that preserves a logical concept across hierarchy enrichment and disambiguates distinct same-title siblings.

recommendations.title: Step 3 (`Add the interactive navigate_concepts walker`) says `--yes` and non-TTY leave sign-off false, and step 8 (`Add
recommendations.body: Step 3 (`Add the interactive navigate_concepts walker`) says `--yes` and non-TTY leave sign-off false, and step 8 (`Add the standalone scope-review command`) tests that such a run persists “every node `signed_off=False`.” On a current tree this clears existing operator approvals even when no state changed, contradicting Architecture §C’s rule that approval is invalidated by a changed decision.
recommendations.suggested_action: Specify that unattended navigation leaves existing sign-off stamps unchanged and marks only newly introduced or state-changed nodes unsigned.

recommendations.title: Step 4 (`Wire the concept sign-off gate into create`) says an unparseable emit should “skip the rest of the gate cleanly
recommendations.body: Step 4 (`Wire the concept sign-off gate into create`) says an unparseable emit should “skip the rest of the gate cleanly — no tree, no overwrite,” and under `--iterate` “an empty fallback is tolerated,” while the Acceptance criteria require the former silent drop to “surface it as a `defer`-suggested concept node.” This failure path finalizes a plan without the machine record or operator gate and can silently discard the very concepts the feature must preserve.
recommendations.suggested_action: require create to retry or stop with an actionable error when concept emission cannot produce a reviewable tree, rather than finalizing an ungated plan

recommendations.title: Step 5 (`Wire the concept sign-off gate into detail`) says “Malformed candidate output is fail-soft for that result,” wh
recommendations.body: Step 5 (`Wire the concept sign-off gate into detail`) says “Malformed candidate output is fail-soft for that result,” while its Acceptance criteria require “Every detail-generation result” to emit everything routed to `## Deferred`. A malformed candidate block can therefore leave deferred prose outside the concept tree and consolidated sign-off, recreating the ungated deferral path the plan promises to eliminate.
recommendations.suggested_action: make an unparseable candidate-deferral block retry or fail the affected detail result before completion so every rendered deferral enters the consolidated tree

recommendations.title: Architecture §C says “Before persisting any changed decision, it invalidates that node’s prior approval,” and Architectu
recommendations.body: Architecture §C says “Before persisting any changed decision, it invalidates that node’s prior approval,” and Architecture §A says sign-off applies to “each node’s own current state,” but step 7 (`Make scope_out_step flip…`) requires an `include → defer` transition to “preserve both” `signed_off` and `signed_off_at`. An unattended `scope-out --apply` can consequently convert an approved inclusion into an approved deferral without operator sign-off on that new state.
recommendations.suggested_action: define the scope-out confirmation as an operator sign-off only on an interactive confirmation path, otherwise clear the flipped node’s approval and surface it through the unsigned-deferral check

recommendations.title: Steps 5 (`Wire concepts into detail…`) and 8 (`Add the standalone scope-review command`) mutate `concepts.json` without
recommendations.body: Steps 5 (`Wire concepts into detail…`) and 8 (`Add the standalone scope-review command`) mutate `concepts.json` without updating plan prose, contradicting Architecture §A’s “tree is source of truth” and Acceptance’s “`## Out of scope` / `## Deferred` plan sections are rendered from the tree.” Step 8’s detail only says “Save the merged tree” and “Render the outcome,” meaning the plan can retain stale scope prose after an operator changes a decision.
recommendations.suggested_action: require every tree-mutating surface to render and transactionally persist the corresponding plan scope sections, or explicitly redefine when and how that one-directional render is synchronized

recommendations.title: Step 5 (`Wire the concept sign-off gate into detail`) performs its consolidated review only after detail bodies have alr
recommendations.body: Step 5 (`Wire the concept sign-off gate into detail`) performs its consolidated review only after detail bodies have already routed candidates to `## Deferred`; if the operator changes a candidate to `include`, the step neither re-authors the affected detail nor removes the deferred text, leaving the supposedly authoritative tree contradicted by the completed artifact.
recommendations.suggested_action: specify how the post-authoring gate applies an `include` decision to affected detail output before the run completes, whether through targeted re-authoring or another explicit incorporation contract.

recommendations.title: step 3 (`Add the interactive navigate_concepts walker`) and step 8 (`Add the standalone scope-review command`) require `
recommendations.body: step 3 (`Add the interactive navigate_concepts walker`) and step 8 (`Add the standalone scope-review command`) require `--yes` or non-TTY execution to leave “every node `signed_off=False`,” but the bundle never distinguishes newly suggested nodes from unchanged nodes carrying an existing operator approval. Re-running `scope-review -y` on a current signed tree can therefore erase valid signoff without any state change or operator decision.
recommendations.suggested_action: specify that unattended runs leave new or changed decisions unsigned while preserving existing signoff stamps on nodes whose state is unchanged

recommendations.title: Architecture §A declares the tree the source of truth and says `state=defer` is “rendered into `## Deferred`” and `state
recommendations.body: Architecture §A declares the tree the source of truth and says `state=defer` is “rendered into `## Deferred`” and `state=wont_do` into “`## Out of scope`,” but only step 4 (`Wire the concept sign-off gate into create`) rewrites those plan sections. Steps 5 (`Wire concepts into detail`) and 8 (`Add the standalone scope-review command`) persist later state changes without re-rendering the plan, leaving the human-facing prose stale and reopening the Risks entry’s “Two sources of truth” failure.
recommendations.suggested_action: Assign every post-create concept mutation a plan-section synchronization contract that atomically re-renders `## Deferred` and `## Out of scope` from the resulting tree and refreshes its fingerprint. - INFO: [rederive-conflicts] Step 8 (`Add the standalone scope-review command`) repeatedly promises “flag-conflicts for operator review,” but neither the tree schema nor the navigator contract defines what constitutes a conflict, how it is represented, or what observable signal forces review. The acceptance test is therefore unfalsifiable. → fix: Define rederive conflict detection and the explicit navigator-visible review state or message that resolves each conflict before sign-off.

recommendations.title: Architecture §H and the structural-remedy Acceptance criterion promise coverage survives split, merge, and re-ground, bu
recommendations.body: Architecture §H and the structural-remedy Acceptance criterion promise coverage survives split, merge, and re-ground, but no implementation step owns the required split feature partitioning or verifies existing actuators provide it; step 7 (`Make scope_out_step flip…`) explicitly defers “The other three structural remedies.” At HEAD, `launcher.py:escalate_to_split` accepts replacements from `create.py:_propose_step_split`, whose response shape omits `features`, so `_apply_step_split` cannot partition the original feature ownership and a formerly covered concept can become uncovered.
recommendations.suggested_action: add an implementation step that makes split replacements preserve or partition the original feature ownership, and explicitly locks in the already-valid merge union and re-ground preservation semantics with remedy-level tests

recommendations.title: Step 8 (`Add the standalone scope-review command`) promises `--rederive` will “flag conflicts for explicit operator revi
recommendations.body: Step 8 (`Add the standalone scope-review command`) promises `--rederive` will “flag conflicts for explicit operator review,” but `ConceptNode` has no conflict field and step 3 (`Add the interactive navigate_concepts walker`) accepts only a `ConceptTree` and displays state, title, hierarchy, and rationale; neither step specifies a transient conflict set, conflict marker, or resolution rule. The command can preserve an old decision while giving the operator no indication that refreshed evidence suggested a different state.
recommendations.suggested_action: specify how re-derivation represents, displays, and requires explicit resolution or acknowledgement of each old-state versus new-suggestion conflict before sign-off

recommendations.title: Architecture §E promises “guaranteed coverage” and the Overview says an included concept “can never be silently dropped,
recommendations.body: Architecture §E promises “guaranteed coverage” and the Overview says an included concept “can never be silently dropped,” while step 6 (`Add the two completeness concept checks…`) explicitly leaves matching to an implementer-selected title/feature slug heuristic and says to “prefer a false negative.” A semantic omission can therefore pass whenever an unrelated committed step shares the concept’s slug, and a real omission can remain silent, so the stated guarantee exceeds the designed signal.
recommendations.suggested_action: narrow the guarantee to the heuristic’s measurable contract or specify an authoritative concept-to-feature ownership signal that makes coverage auditable without semantic false negatives
